children: The Bank of Korea is widely expected to leave its policy rate unchanged at Thursday's policy meeting, pausing after back-to-back rate increases in July and August, a poll shows. All 23 economists surveyed by The Wall Street Journal expect the BOK to hold the rate at 3.00%, with most forecasting another rate hike before the end of 2027. Some expect the BOK to maintain its hawkish stance by allowing a few board members to dissent in favor of a rate hike, citing stronger economic growth forecasts and elevated core inflation in the country. "We expect the BOK's hawkish rhetoric to persist," says Nomura economist Jeong Woo Park. Nomura maintains its forecast for rate hikes in November this year and February next year. (kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)
